title: Lumbar disc units in axial compression - Markolf & Morris 1974 (JBJS 56A:675) MIN, average and MAX curves (secondary, Ghezelbash 2020a Fig 4a)

quantity.name: axial compression force-displacement curve
quantity.definition: axial compressive force vs axial displacement; MIN, average (AVE) and MAX curves as plotted by Ghezelbash 2020a

source.authors: Ghezelbash F, Shirazi-Adl A, Baghani M, Eskandari AH
source.sample: not stated in the secondary source (see primary: Markolf KL, Morris JM 1974, JBJS Am 56:675-687, doi 10.2106/00004623-197456040-00003); human lumbar intervertebral discs with adjacent vertebral bodies tested in axial compression

protocol.summary: Axial compression of disc specimens (Markolf & Morris 1974, structural components of the disc); rate and preload not given in the secondary source.
how_to_simulate: Model a lumbar disc with adjacent vertebral bodies
Apply axial compression slowly from zero load to about 4000 N
Report the force at each displacement; compare with AVE and the MIN-MAX range
protocol.notes: Secondary data: digitised from a figure of Ghezelbash et al. 2020a (the owner's FE validation band; also Fig 2c of Ghezelbash 2025 bioRxiv). Primary paper not in the repository. Points below 0.4 mm omitted: the three red curves overlap Brown, Tencer and Marini there. n must be checked in the primary paper.

extraction.from: Ghezelbash 2020a Fig 4a (red dash-dot = MIN, red solid = AVE, red dashed = MAX); same data form the 'Experiment' band of Ghezelbash 2025 bioRxiv Fig 2c
extraction.uncertainty: +/-0.01 mm, +/-30 N; where curves overlap below 0.3 mm: +/-60 N
extraction.check_notes: Page rendered at 600 dpi; axes from tick marks (831 px/mm, 0.302 px/N); curves found by colour (green = Brown, red = Markolf & Morris, lime squares = Asano) in column scans every 0.025-0.1 mm, line style (solid/dashed/dash-dot) assigned by continuity and checked against a gridded zoom. Values are the review authors' plot of the primary data, not the primary paper.

pass_rule.rule: model curve inside the min-max envelope (or within +/-25% of the curve)
